### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s).

**41** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 06881565bdced6c949f05d59f0059a3ff7409924`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 06881565bdced6c949f05d59f0059a3ff7409924` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2be4faf22c491ddabe4c8430a1b493aabf6aa216` — the merge of head `424e92959b28d0338b269e7452de3c3fc994fad6` into base `06881565bdced6c949f05d59f0059a3ff7409924`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2be4faf22c491ddabe4c8430a1b493aabf6aa216 && git checkout 2be4faf22c491ddabe4c8430a1b493aabf6aa216
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 06881565bdced6c949f05d59f0059a3ff7409924 424e92959b28d0338b269e7452de3c3fc994fad6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 06881565bdced6c949f05d59f0059a3ff7409924 && git merge --no-ff 424e92959b28d0338b269e7452de3c3fc994fad6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 06881565bdced6c949f05d59f0059a3ff7409924
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 06881565bdced6c949f05d59f0059a3ff7409924` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `424e92959b28d0338b269e7452de3c3fc994fad6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/identity-objects-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/owner-fixed-rule.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/personal-view-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/user-preference-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/user-preference-hooks.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/user-preference-owner-fixed.dogfood.test.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user-preference.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/manifest.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/identity-write-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/system-write-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-hook-dispatch.ts, packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts, ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/userState.ts, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx (row 26c, read), .changeset/29630-user-preference-owner-fixed.md (read for ②)

Narrowing face on card #29630, a security card. Per the security-findings rule (triage 6590532575, #29111) this record states the rule the PR restores and the judgments of it, and nothing of mechanism, reproduction or path. Read: the card body and all six comments (triage, two claims, two dev reports, the hand-off), the PR body, its file list, the net diff against `main` at this head, the check-runs on this head, and the precedent record 6590198210 on PR #29575. The cited code was read on `origin/main`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**The rule the PR restores.** A `sys_user_preference` row's owner is fixed when the row is saved: a non-system update that sends a `user_id` other than the stored one is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, for a member, an organization administrator and a platform administrator alike; an update that echoes the stored owner or does not send it saves as before; a system write is not judged. It is the rule PR #29575 gave `sys_personal_view`, now held by one shared check.

| Change the diff implies | Judgment |
|:--|:--|
| New `beforeUpdate` rule on `sys_user_preference`, refusing a change of `user_id` for every non-system caller | **Right.** It is the shape the card asks for (step 2), the shape the precedent ruled right on `main` for the twin object, and the reason row 26c already states on `main` applies to this object as written (`sys-user-preference.object.ts` declares the same owner-column `defaultRowScope`, `user_id` is a plain lookup, and no hook on `main` names the object). The refusal is judged before any write, keeps the ADR-0112 pair, names the row and the column and echoes no other id (pinned). |
| An echo of the stored owner, or a payload without `user_id`, is not judged | **Right.** The console's own writer (`userState.ts`) updates `{ value }` only and creates in the caller's name, so the one shipped consumer is untouched; the echo control is pinned at both levels. |
| The system skip (`ctx.session.isSystem === true`) | **Right as a platform-writer skip.** No shipped system writer updates this object (`git grep` on `main`: no `src` writer names it outside its object file, the permission sets and the manifest). The same incompleteness the precedent named as its S1 is carried over unchanged; see ④. |
| Every non-system update dispatch reaches the rule with `ctx.previous` bound | **Right on `main`.** The by-id path binds the prior row before the before-phase dispatch; the predicate (`multi`) path dispatches per matched row with that row as `previous` (`engine-hook-dispatch.ts`); the REST import and batch run under the caller's own context. The rule's `!previous` early return therefore never admits a non-system change on a shipped path. Unchanged from the precedent's reading. |
| `sys_personal_view` moved onto the shared check | **Right, behaviour-preserving.** `isOwnerChange` is the inline predicate verbatim (same `sameId` normalisation, same `sets` test, same system skip), `ownerFixedError` with `{ label: 'Personal view', noun: 'view' }` renders the former message byte-for-byte, and the call sits at the same point of `validateOnUpdate`, before the config check. The `ctx.object` guard stays in the caller, so `assertOwnerUnchanged` is never reached for another object. The 10 skipped and 3703 passing plugin-auth tests on the dev report include `personal-view-hooks.test.ts` unchanged. |
| `ownerChangeError` removed from `personal-view-hooks.ts`; `owner-fixed-rule.ts` and `user-preference-hooks.ts` added | **No public surface moves.** Neither module is reachable from `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts` or the package `exports` on `main` or on this head, and `ownerChangeError` has no consumer on `main` outside its own file. |
| Registration in `AuthPlugin.start` and `IdentityObjectsPlugin.start`, under distinct `packageId`s | **Right.** It mirrors the personal-view registration line for line, so the rule travels with the table on both kernels; `IdentityObjectsPlugin.init()` refuses a composition beside `AuthPlugin` on `main`, so the hook is never bound twice. The comment's claim that the manifest registers both objects is true (`manifest.ts` lists `SysUserPreference` and `SysPersonalView`). |
| Row 26c of `system-context.mdx` widened to both objects, anchor moved to `owner-fixed-rule.ts#isOwnerChange`, register row regenerated | **Right in substance**; `check:system-context-census` is green on this head (Lint, docs and code guards). |
| Unit pins (`user-preference-hooks.test.ts`) | **Hold the rule on its own**: three callers refused, message shape, clearing the owner refused, four controls, and the registration shape (one `beforeUpdate` hook, nothing on create or delete). The fake-engine harness is right for a hook whose whole input is the context. |
| REST pins (`user-preference-owner-fixed.dogfood.test.ts`) | **Right in shape**: three callers refused on their own row, two administrators do not reach a member's row by id, echo and value-only controls. Note: the dogfood job in `ci.yml` is push/schedule-gated, so on this PR head the three shards are `skipped` and the only reading of these pins is the dev's local battery on the card (6592969538: 400 files, 3304 tests, 0 failures). Not re-judged here; the push run after merge is the CI reading. |
| Dev's claim that the platform-admin REST pin stays green when the registration is ablated | Not re-judged (read-only). It makes no claim the record relies on: the unit pin holds the rule for that caller. |

**Check-runs on this head, as read**: 49 runs; 31 `success`, 12 `skipped` (opt-in, matrix-gated or ui-path-gated, the dogfood shards among them), none failed, and 6 pending at the time of the last read, all of them `Test Core` shards (7/8 and 8/8 had already concluded `success`). Green: Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, Type Check (debt ledger, consumer, source), Lint (ESLint, PM dispatch-gates, docs and code guards, CI/release/engine gates, query-options erasure, tooling self-tests), Live E2E UI, Test UI, Dogfood Regression Gate (umbrella). The seat lands only once Test Core concludes; nothing in this diff touches a core package other than plugin-auth, whose own suite the dev ran green on this head.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch` holds.** `Metadata-protocol: none` is true (no key, value, type or default an author writes against moves), and AGENTS.md's rule is that a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition; the precedent (#29575) shipped the same rule at `patch`. The changeset carries the banner, both declaration lines and exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, and `Check Changeset` is green.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` holds.** The line answers whether the card widens the accept set or the public surface (`clause2-line.mjs`): it does neither. One accepted write is now refused on one object, no export, route, object or type is added, and the only removed symbol is module-internal. The card body's `yes (narrowing)` was the filing seat's guess; both claims and the precedent's reading correct it, and `(narrowing)` is the arm that carries BREAKING either way.
- No `@objectstack/platform-objects` line is needed: the object file is unchanged.
- The changeset prose matches the tree: now, unchanged, shared rule, who sees it, remedy. The remedy sentence is the one the error message gives.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Dev deviation 1 (one commit beyond the hand-off, comment and changeset wording only)**: verified; `424e9295` touches the shared rule's header comment and one changeset line, no code. Right, and the trim to the rule alone is what triage 6590532575 asks.

**Dev deviation 2 (PR template headings folded into the os-dev order)**: prose, not reviewed.

**Dev deviation 3 (`no (narrowing)`, not `yes`)**: right; ② above.

**Dev deviation in the hand-off (the delta's engine-rig shape not used for the unit pins)**: accepted; the fake-engine harness is the right instrument for a context-only hook, and the real-stack face is the REST file.

**Open question, step 3 of the card (the class: close per object here, or one platform-level card for the update floor)**: **escalated to the seat, with this reading of `main` in support of the dev's option B.** Every other platform object whose default row scope is its own `user_id` column lives in the `better-auth` bucket, whose user-context writes `identity-write-guard.ts` refuses outright; `member_default` grants `allowEdit` on exactly `sys_user`, `sys_user_preference` and `sys_personal_view`; so the shipped population the rule has to close is the two `system-data` objects, and this PR closes the second. What the per-object rule cannot reach is an app-authored object scoped on its own owner column, which is the platform-level question the dev names. The dev's census itself is off-board and was not read. `Fixes #29630` is right if the seat files the floor card through the advisory channel; otherwise `Part of`.

**Open question in the hand-off (closing keyword)**: the same answer.

**Escalated**: the step-3 ruling, above. Nothing else.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main`: the object's own docblock, `defaultRowScope` and row 26c all declare a preference as the user's own row, and no spec, skill or doc on `main` offers changing a saved preference's owner as a capability (`Skills-docs: none` in the PR body is true; the one page that names the rule is row 26c, updated here). So the refusal makes the object's own declared posture real at the consumer rather than taking a declared capability away. The consumer that exists (`userState.ts`) never sends `user_id` on an update. Nothing declared and undelivered is being narrowed around.

I tried to break the rule four ways, each read in the cited code on `main` and found closed: a dispatch without `previous` (none on a non-system path, ① above); a second registrar binding it twice (refused at `init`); a bulk payload diverging per row (the batch payload is one, judged per matched row); and a value that normalises to the stored id (the `sameId` normalisation treats only `undefined`, `null` and `''` as the same absent value, and an echo is the declared no-change). A private finding was not needed: no further gap was found on this head.

**Must-fix**: none.

**Should-fix**
- **S1 (carried from the precedent's S1 on #29575, still unapplied on `main`).** Row 26c, `owner-fixed-rule.ts`, `personal-view-hooks.ts` and `user-preference-hooks.ts` describe the system skip only as "no shipped system writer does". The precedent record asked for one sentence saying the rule does not bind app-authored automation elevated to system, the family row 1b's `flow-system-identity-write-refusal.ts` names, so the row says what is really lost. This PR widens the row to a second object and copies the sentence; it is the place to add the one line, for both objects at once. Docs and comments only; no behaviour change.
- **S2 (carried from the precedent's S2).** `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/manifest.ts` still says `sys_personal_view`'s "save validation and default flag live in personal-view-hooks.ts"; the default flag is gone, the owner rule now lives in `owner-fixed-rule.ts`, and the adjacent `SysUserPreference` entry names no rule. One comment.
- **S3.** `user-preference-hooks.ts`'s docblock says "a create is the row scope's (a preference created in another member's name is refused there)". True on `main` for the member, and the precedent pinned it for the twin object, but this PR carries no create pin for `sys_user_preference`. Either add the one REST control or drop the parenthesis; the rule under review is the update rule and is unaffected.

None of the three changes the accept set or is a reason to hold the PR.
